name: @media-router/plugin-mpegts-muxer
description: Multi-program MPEG-TS muxer — combines N video and M audio MPEG-TS sources into a single transport stream

mediaRouter.description: Combines several muxed/mpegts streams into one — pick any number of video and audio inputs.

videoStreams.description: Video input streams — "+ Add" creates another input port. Each name is broadcast in-band (stream-info channel) so a downstream demuxer labels its output; blank falls back to the connected source module's name.

audioStreams.description: Audio input streams — "+ Add" creates another input port. Each name is broadcast in-band (stream-info channel) so a downstream demuxer labels its output; blank falls back to the connected source module's name.

language.description: ISO 639 language code (2/3-letter, e.g. en / eng / deu) written into the output PMT as this stream's language descriptor — the standard signalling every receiver understands. Blank passes the source stream's own language through unchanged. Applied at pipeline build — changing it restarts the muxer.

offsetMs.description: Lipsync offset for this audio input on the mux timeline. Negative advances audio — set to minus the measured audio-late skew to cancel a stable path delay with no added latency (costs ~|offset| of clipped audio at pipeline start). Re-measure after changing audio-path buffering. Applied at pad-link time — changing it restarts the muxer.

alignment.description: MPEG-TS muxer alignment — keep at SRT-aligned for SRT/RIST/UDP transport. Use Continuous only for v1-style receivers that derive timing from byte flow (their tsparse mis-estimates bitrate from 1316 B bursts)

queueLeaky.description: Input queue behaviour. OFF (non-leaky): never drop — hold the leading stream up to Queue depth while waiting out A/V skew or a stall; backlog flushes after recovery (contribution/stability). ON (leaky): shed the oldest frame once Queue depth of backlog builds, so output resumes at the live edge immediately after a stall (live production). Queues sit upstream of the muxer, after the codec parser — drops always land on whole frames; the mux output itself is never queued (a drop there would corrupt the TS mid-frame).

queueDepthMs.description: Input queue bound. Non-leaky: how much A/V arrival skew to absorb without back-pressuring (set ≥ the worst skew of your wiring: transcode chain ~200 ms, demuxer audio pacing 160 ms, B-frame delay ~120 ms). Leaky: how much backlog to tolerate before shedding starts.

emitStreamInfo.description: Broadcast the in-band stream-info channel (names + codec info for streams MPEG-TS can't signal natively) on the private metadata PID 0x1f0, with the PCR pinned to the first media stream. Natively-signalled data (codec stream types, language descriptors) is always on the wire regardless. Turn off only for strict external receivers that reject unknown private PIDs.
